inputs.wacc_rationale: WACC 10.5% NZD-built (flows are NZD): NZ 10y govt ~4.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta 1.1 = 10.5% base cost of equity + 2.5pp premium for the structural risks the parent brief assigns to the discount rate (BayWa's ~74% stake under a stalled distressed-sale process, ~20% JWM block, minimal NZX free float/liquidity, sub-NZ$300m market cap, single-region weather catastrophe exposure) = ~13% CoE; Kd 6% pre-tax / 4.3% after; E/D 70/30 at market -> 10.4%, rounded to 10.5%. Charged ONCE: the same WACC in all three scenarios, and the scenario flows carry only OPERATING outcomes (crop/weather, margin, growth) -- governance and liquidity risk are not re-charged in the weights (owner-fcf.md s7f).
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US/cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + section 7) applied to the CONTINUING business only (Apples + VentureFruit + retained Australian T&G Fresh rump), 10-year component build, BLENDED 50/50 with a history-disciplined asset leg (parent book value x exit P/B calibrated to T&G's own 10-year P/B range). The blend was applied as the sanity-check fix: the pure earnings leg implied 0.2x book against a 10-year floor of 0.42x, i.e. it valued NZ$232m of land and buildings at valuation and the orchard estate at a fraction of what any buyer has paid. The ticker straddles two routing rows (operating company / asset-backed land owner under a live 74%-stake sale process); the parts are valued separately and blended, as the routing table requires when a business straddles rows. Fresh build -- no prior TGG.NZ DCF.

CONTINUING-OPS BASE: FY0 = FY2025 re-presented continuing operations from the H1-2026 interim report (income statement + note 3): revenue 1,144.643m, operating profit 28.876m, D&A 42.003m -> EBITDA 70.879m (6.2%). The CSV's FY2019-FY2025 rows are WHOLE-COMPANY; FY2025 group revenue 1,558.7m includes 414.1m of discontinued revenue (note 7). H1-2026 572.3m vs re-presented H1-2025 557.9m = +2.6% like-for-like; the CSV's H1 FY2025 920.6m is as-reported and must not be compared. H1-2026 continuing operating profit 11.6m (+30.3%); NPAT -30.5m is dominated by the -34.4m IFRS-5 remeasurement of the disposal group, continuing NPAT was -0.9m.

OWNER FCF: last_fcf 2.5m = FY2025 CONTINUING owner FCF, derived as continuing OCF (91.948 group - 25.916 discontinued = 66.0) - continuing capex (~30, group 32.6 less the disposal group's ~3) - continuing lease cash (~33.5 of the group's 41.9). reported_fcf 59.326 is the GROUP figure and is a peak: capex was suppressed to 32.6m (vs 48-107m FY2021-24) and OCF carried a 6.9m debtor release. SBC = 0 (no share-based payment scheme disclosed in any filing; SBC rows kept explicit at 0%). Interest income (2.5m, on grower loans/cash) is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt, so no cash pile is being counted twice.

LEASES: treatment (B) -- leases as operating cost. Lease cash (group 41.9m FY2025 total lease outflow per note 12, ~80% continuing by ROU-asset share = ~33.5m = 2.9% of continuing revenue) is charged inside the flows as lease_cost_pct; lease liabilities (210.7m Dec-25; 165.6m continuing + 42.5m in the disposal group at Jun-26) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A (1.75%) is owned-asset D&A only (continuing D&A 42.0m less ~22m ROU depreciation); the EBITDA margin driver is on the reported post-IFRS-16 basis with the lease cash then deducted explicitly -- do not read the 9% mature margin as pre-rent.

NET DEBT: 69.654m pro forma = Dec-2025 audited borrowings 194.840 - cash 47.618 - term deposits 1.510 (= 145.712) less expected T&G Fresh disposal proceeds 76.058 (disposal group assets 143.904 - liabilities 67.846, remeasured to fair value less costs to sell, H1-2026 note 6; the note's 84.338 'net assets held for sale' ALSO includes the 8.280m Ettrick property, carried here as a non-operating asset instead; proceeds earmarked for debt repayment incl. the 20.8m BayWa loan). Dec-31 is the seasonal trough and matches a Y1=FY2026 build; the Jun-2026 figure (307.9 borrowings - 72.7 cash = 235.3m) is the seasonal PEAK with the 109m seasonal facility drawn against 108m of harvested inventory and 55.7m grower advances -- using it would double-charge working capital already in the flows. If the Commerce Commission blocks the Turner sale, net debt is 76m higher but the discontinued business's ~10.8m NPAT / 25.9m OCF stays -- roughly value-neutral at 8x, so all three scenarios assume completion.

NCI: charged ONCE, in the flows -- the NCI profit share (5.8m FY2025, Worldwide Fruit UK 50% = 2.8m + immaterial subsidiaries 3.0m; ALL inside continuing operations, which is why continuing EPS was -0.4c in FY2025 on +5.3m continuing NPAT) is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax + leakage driver: NZ 28% statutory cash tax ramping from ~10% (37.5m deferred tax assets = ~5 years of shelter) plus NCI leakage falling from ~20% of EBIT to ~10% as Apples earnings outgrow the stable UK distributor. The 18.7m book NCI is NOT deducted in the bridge (it would double-charge and understates the stream anyway). Calibration: FY0 continuing EBIT pre-IFRS-16 ~17.4m less bank interest ~15.8m plus other income ~5m = PBT 6.5m reported; less tax 1.3m and NCI 5.8m = -0.5m attributable = reported -0.4c continuing EPS.

WACC 10.5% NZD-built (flows are NZD): NZ 10y govt ~4.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta 1.1 = 10.5% base cost of equity + 2.5pp premium for the structural risks the parent brief assigns to the discount rate (BayWa's ~74% stake under a stalled distressed-sale process, ~20% JWM block, minimal NZX free float/liquidity, sub-NZ$300m market cap, single-region weather catastrophe exposure) = ~13% CoE; Kd 6% pre-tax / 4.3% after; E/D 70/30 at market -> 10.4%, rounded to 10.5%. Charged ONCE: the same WACC in all three scenarios, and the scenario flows carry only OPERATING outcomes (crop/weather, margin, growth) -- governance and liquidity risk are not re-charged in the weights (owner-fcf.md s7f).

ASSET LEG: parent book value per share 3.66 (Jun-2026, 448.6m attributable equity; parent NTA 3.30 after 44.2m intangibles; the company's reported NTA of 3.53 at Dec-25 INCLUDES the 18.1m NCI) x exit P/B by scenario: bear 0.45x (FY2023-24 trough 0.42-0.46x), base 0.70x (10y average ex-FY2023 0.73x, rounded down), bull 0.95x (FY2017-18 0.86-0.97x; a control transaction at ~book). The stock has traded above 1.0x book only once in ten year-ends (FY2016, 1.14x) -- the history disciplines the bull leg. Land and buildings carried at fair value (232m, independent valuers, FY2025 KAM) and the maturing ENVY orchard estate are what the leg represents; the sale of a 74% stake under the NZ Takeovers Code (equal-price offer to all holders) is the live route by which minorities realise asset value.

TERMINAL: cap 12x owner FCF (10x bear) -- agricultural cyclical, thin margins; Gordon at 2.5% exceeds the cap in the base so the cap binds. Horizon 10 years because the margin is still ramping at year 5.

The sliders move the going-concern leg at 100% weight, so displayed slider sensitivity is 2x the blended value's true sensitivity (asset_weight 0.5). PRICE 2.40 is a regular NZX close (4-Sep-2026), not an after-hours print; NZX liquidity in TGG is minimal (free float ~6%) so closes can gap on tiny volume.

historical_growth.basis: WHOLE-COMPANY (pre-divestment) basis for every FY row; the continuing business is ~73% of FY2025 revenue and ~64% of FY2025 EBITDA, so none of these CAGRs describes the go-forward company
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: analyst judgment on the CONTINUING Apples/VentureFruit business: Apples revenue +6.2% H1-2026 (550.9 vs 518.9), NZ crop volume +24% in 2026 from maturing ENVY plantings, premium-apple category ~8% CAGR (company/industry forecast) haircut for size/grade mix and UK/EU oversupply. NOT derived from any historical CAGR -- see notes
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (parent book -0.6% 5yr, -4.4% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (+2.0% 5yr, +6.1% 3yr) and EPS CAGR is negative: the FY2022-23 losses (cyclone, orchard write-downs) consumed book value while revenue grew. Owner FCF was negative in 6 of the last 7 years (replanting capex + IFRS-16 lease principal) so an FCF CAGR is undefined. The H1-2026 revenue print (572.3) vs the CSV's H1-2025 (920.6) is a DIVESTMENT re-presentation, not a decline; like-for-like continuing growth was +2.6%.

scenario_narratives.base: Turner/Bidfood/Unearthed sales complete and 84m of proceeds cut net debt to ~70m. Apples grows 6%/yr FY27-30 as ENVY plantings mature (NZ crop +24% in 2026), JOLI launches in Vietnam and the NZ-India FTA opens a new market, then decelerates to 3%. Group EBITDA margin (post-IFRS-16) climbs from 7.0% in FY2026 to 9.0% by FY2031 as stranded corporate cost in the 'Other' segment (-45m FY2025) is cut and VentureFruit reaches breakeven; capex normalises to 3% of revenue (~35m) between the suppressed FY2025 (32.6m) and the FY2024 48m. Cash tax ramps to 28% as the 37.5m deferred tax asset is used; NCI leakage fades from 20% to 10% of EBIT. Asset leg at 0.70x book, the 10-year average.
scenario_narratives.bull: Apples 2035 strategy delivers: 8% growth FY27-29 on ENVY US household penetration (12% -> 15%), China/Vietnam/Thailand volume (+26/+34/+10% H1-26) and India; VentureFruit's royalty model (California Giant berries, Chinese PVR wins) turns profitable; corporate cost-out takes the group EBITDA margin to 11.5% by FY2032. BayWa's stake is sold to a strategic buyer who, under the Takeovers Code, offers all holders ~0.95x book -- the asset leg at FY2017-18 multiples.
scenario_narratives.bear: El Nino delivers the weather event flagged in the H1-2026 outlook: FY2027 revenue -10% and EBITDA margin 3.5% (a milder Gabrielle), recovering to a 6.5% ceiling as UK/EU oversupply and retailer buying power cap pricing; capex stays at 3.3% because replanting cannot be deferred; NCI leakage stays high because the UK distributor's profit does not fall with the NZ crop. Terminal cap 10x, terminal growth 2%. The BayWa process drags with no offer and the stock stays at its FY2023-24 trough of 0.45x book on the asset leg.

bear.zero_floor_note: Owner FCF is negative in all ten years and the terminal value sits on the zero floor: on this path the continuing business does not survive as a going concern and the value is the asset leg alone (a real owner sells the orchards). Flagged per owner-fcf.md s4.

entry_price.method: Price at which the base-case blended value returns a 15% IRR: PV at 15% of the 10 owner-FCF years + terminal value REBUILT at 15% (min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF10)) discounted at 15% + the same side term (non-operating investments + asset-realisation blend, a today-value) - pro forma net debt, per share. Computed for all three scenarios and probability-weighted.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (cap re-applied). 10.5% row = valuation.base.intrinsic_value; 15% row = entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Blended value per share; the asset leg is held at its base value so only the going-concern leg moves

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (vs house 15%): a single-region agricultural business one El Nino away from a repeat of FY2023, a majority owner in a German debt restructuring that must sell, a Commerce Commission gate on the divestment, and continuing-ops attributable earnings of roughly zero in a GOOD apple year. Base 50%. Bull 20% (vs house 35%): the bull leg needs three independent things -- the Apples 2035 margin step-up, the corporate cost-out AND a control transaction near book -- and the stock has closed above 1.0x book once in ten years.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero filer: house and street bases coincide, so the accounting-regime band collapses to a point; band_position is null by construction, not 0%.

sanity_check.basis: Yahoo TGG.NZ monthly closes (range=10y), December bar = FY-end close, FY2016-FY2025. P/B on PARENT book (total equity less NCI; FY2016-18 from the FY2020 five-year review). P/E on reported attributable EPS (cents). EV/EBITDA on the as-stored group basis (mkt cap + borrowings + IFRS-16 leases - cash) / group EBITDA post-IFRS-16, available FY2019+ only. P/Sales on group revenue. All WHOLE-COMPANY; FY2023 (Cyclone Gabrielle, EBITDA 13.1m, EPS -41.7c) excluded from averages but kept in the table.
trip_tests: implied P/E > 2x avg (only where earnings are meaningful)
ASSET FLOOR: implied P/B < 10y min while price sits in the lower half of the 10y range
trip_reasons_dcf_only: ASSET-FLOOR TRIP: implied P/B 0.26x is BELOW the 10y minimum 0.42x (FY2024 trough) -- the pure earnings model values NZ$232m of land and buildings at valuation, and the orchard estate, at less than the market has ever paid for them
sanity_check.pe_test: NOT MEANINGFUL: attributable EPS was 0.7c, -4.4c, -41.7c, -13.0c and 8.3c in five of the last seven years, so historical P/E is degenerate (ranges 11x to 413x). Judged on P/B, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales.
sanity_check.diagnosis: The pure going-concern DCF on continuing operations gives 0.96/share (0.26x book, 4.3x FY2025 group EV/EBITDA, 0.075x sales) -- BELOW every multiple the market has paid in ten years, including the FY2024 trough (0.42x book, 0.15x sales). The diagnosis is not that the flows are wrong: the continuing business really did earn ~-0.5m attributable in FY2025 after leases, interest and NCI. It is that an earnings model assigns no value to NZ$232m of land and buildings at independent valuation and a maturing ENVY orchard estate that a control buyer (BayWa must sell 74%; the Takeovers Code makes any acquirer offer all holders) or a liquidating owner would realise. The under-valuation trip is therefore the asset-floor trip, and the fix is the blended earnings/asset model the routing table prescribes when a business straddles rows.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Blended 50/50 with an asset leg = parent book value/share 3.66 x exit P/B disciplined by the 10y history (bear 0.45x / base 0.70x / bull 0.95x; 10y avg ex-FY2023 0.73x, min 0.42x, max 1.14x). Base blended IV 1.76 -> implied P/B 0.48x, inside the historical band; EV/EBITDA 5.2x vs 10y avg 7.23x; P/Sales 0.138x vs 10y avg 0.28x. No over-valuation test trips on either basis.

no_re_rate_reference.note: Memo: the price the 10y average multiples would put on the continuing business today (not a replacement for the house value)

valuation_philosophy.model: Owner-FCF DCF on continuing operations (10-year component build, IFRS-16 leases as operating cost, NCI as leakage in the flows) blended 50/50 with an asset leg (parent book x history-disciplined exit P/B).
valuation_philosophy.why_not_pure_dcf: Every FY row in the metrics history is on the pre-divestment whole-company basis, reported FCF is IFRS-16-flattered and FY2025's +59.3m sits on a suppressed capex year, so no historical FCF series can be extrapolated. Rebuilt from the H1-2026 re-presented continuing operations, the going-concern leg shows a business that earned roughly zero for the parent in a good apple year: EBITDA 70.9m less ~33.5m lease cash, ~20m owned-asset D&A, ~16m bank interest and 5.8m NCI. A DCF of that stream (0.8/share) values the company's land, buildings and orchards at ~0.2x book, below anything the market has paid in a decade -- which is a statement about what the earnings model omits, not about the assets.
valuation_philosophy.why_the_asset_leg: Land and buildings are carried at independent valuation (232m); the ENVY/JAZZ orchard estate and PVR rights are real; BayWa (~74%) is a forced seller and the NZ Takeovers Code means any buyer of that stake must offer minorities the same price. The asset leg is what that route realises. It is disciplined, not aspirational: exit P/B is capped at what TGG itself has traded at -- above 1.0x book once in ten year-ends, 0.42x at the FY2024 trough, 0.73x on average.
valuation_philosophy.why_50_50: Two mutually exclusive outcomes for a minority holder: continue as a thinly-profitable apple grower (earnings leg) or a change-of-control/asset realisation (asset leg). Neither has a decisive edge in probability over a 3-5 year horizon, and the weight is held constant across scenarios so scenario differences come only from the drivers and the exit P/B.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_fix: Applied. Trip: implied P/B below the 10-year minimum on the pure DCF. Fix: the blend above. Post-fix implied multiples sit inside the historical band on every test.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_it: A Commerce Commission block (net debt +76m, discontinued earnings retained -- roughly neutral); an El Nino crop failure (bear case, 30% weight); a firm offer for the BayWa stake (moves the asset weight and exit P/B toward the bull leg); FY2026 results showing the 'Other' segment loss shrinking below -35m (raises the base margin path).
valuation_philosophy.risk_placement: Structural risks (BayWa distress, JWM block, illiquidity, weather catastrophe, sub-300m cap) are charged ONCE, in a 2.5pp WACC premium; scenario flows and weights carry operating outcomes only.

methodology.lease_treatment: B: lease cash in flows, lease liabilities excluded from net debt
